rationale: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they didn't regroup the 13 ones into 1 ten and 3 ones. The place-value / make-a-ten model specifically demonstrates bundling 10 ones into a ten rod, leaving the remaining ones behind.
intent: Demonstrate make-a-ten on the place-value with values [14]. Tutor points at: 10 ones bundling into 1 ten rod

frames.caption: Here are 14 ones. That is too many for the ones place: it can only hold 0 to 9.
Bundle ten of them. Ten ones make one ten, so the bundle moves to the tens place. 4 ones are left.
Write 1 in the tens place and 4 in the ones place: 14. One digit per place.

judgement.reasoning: The student wrote 513 for 37 + 26 because they do not understand that two-digit sums in the ones column must be regrouped (10 ones bundled into 1 ten). The demo specifically illustrates that 14 ones cannot fit in the ones column (only digits 0 to 9 can) and shows 10 ones bundling into 1 ten and moving over, leaving 4 ones. This directly addresses the underlying place-value obstacle.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this is an excellent, direct worked example showing why a two-digit ones total must be bundled into tens and ones before writing the answer.
